config.title: useSyncExternalStore

intro.title: useSyncExternalStore
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that displays a live counter. You will learn how to use the useSyncExternalStore hook to subscribe to and read from an external data store. This involves understanding how to create a store, subscribe to its changes, and get its current snapshot. The main technologies used are React, TypeScript, and the useSyncExternalStore hook for managing external state efficiently.
intro.usecase: The useSyncExternalStore hook is essential for connecting React components to non-React state sources, such as browser APIs, third-party libraries, or global stores. In real-world applications, this pattern powers live dashboards that sync with external data feeds, collaborative tools that reflect real-time user presence, and media players that update UI based on native playback events. Developers use it to ensure UI consistency when integrating with WebSocket connections, browser storage, or custom observable libraries, making it a key tool for building responsive, data-driven interfaces.

objectives: Implement a basic external store with getState, subscribe, and unsubscribe functions
Configure useSyncExternalStore to connect a React component to an external store
Manipulate store state through controlled actions and observe component updates
Initialize a React component that renders synchronized data from an external source
Construct a subscription mechanism that triggers re-renders when store data changes
Integrate useSyncExternalStore with TypeScript to enforce type-safe store interactions
Apply useSyncExternalStore to synchronize UI with non-React state management systems

steps.title: Import React and useSyncExternalStore
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary APIs from the React library.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have the necessary imports to use React and the useSyncExternalStore hook.
successCriteria: React and useSyncExternalStore are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useSyncExternalStore from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Please import React and useSyncExternalStore from 'react'.

steps.title: Create a simple external store
steps.instruction: Create a simple external store object named 'store' with a 'value' property (number) and 'subscribe' and 'unsubscribe' functions.
steps.hint: Define an object with a value property and functions that manage subscriptions. The subscribe function should accept a callback and return an unsubscribe function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A store object is defined with a value property and subscription functions, ready to be used with useSyncExternalStore.
successCriteria: The store object has a 'value' property (number), a 'subscribe' function that accepts a callback and returns an unsubscribe function, and an 'unsubscribe' function or mechanism.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your store has a value property and both subscribe and unsubscribe functions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store object is missing required properties or functions. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Define the store interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'Store' with three properties: 'value' of type number, 'subscribe' of type (listener: () => void) => () => void, and 'getSnapshot' of type () => number.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with their types.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TypeScript interface named 'Store' with the correct property types is added to the code.
successCriteria: The Store interface is defined with 'value: number', 'subscribe: (listener: () => void) => () => void', and 'getSnapshot: () => number' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined an interface, but check the property names and types. The Store interface needs 'value: number', 'subscribe: (listener: () => void) => () => void', and 'getSnapshot: () => number'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Store interface is not correctly defined. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword with the correct property types.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named StoreDisplay with proper TypeScript typing. The component should return null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called StoreDisplay that returns null. Remember to add TypeScript typing for the component.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named StoreDisplay is created with proper TypeScript typing and returns null.
successCriteria: StoreDisplay component is defined as a function or arrow function with TypeScript typing and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a component named StoreDisplay with proper TypeScript typing that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you've defined a function or arrow function named StoreDisplay with TypeScript typing that returns null.

steps.title: Use useSyncExternalStore to connect to the store
steps.instruction: Inside your StoreDisplay component, call useSyncExternalStore to subscribe to the external store and get its current snapshot.
steps.hint: Call useSyncExternalStore with two arguments: the store's subscribe function and the store's getSnapshot function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: subscribing to a store
const currentValue = useSyncExternalStore(store.subscribe, store.getSnapshot);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will be able to read the current value from the external store.
successCriteria: useSyncExternalStore is called with store.subscribe and store.getSnapshot as arguments.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're passing both store.subscribe and store.getSnapshot to useSyncExternalStore.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try calling useSyncExternalStore with the store's subscribe and getSnapshot functions as arguments.

steps.title: Display the store value in the component
steps.instruction: Inside the StoreDisplay component, return JSX that displays the current store value retrieved from useSyncExternalStore.
steps.hint: Use the value variable you got from useSyncExternalStore in the previous step. Return a paragraph or heading element that shows this value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will render the current store value (0) on the screen.
successCriteria: The StoreDisplay component returns JSX that includes the value variable inside curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning JSX that includes the value variable from useSyncExternalStore.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return JSX that displays the store value. Check that you're using the value variable inside your returned JSX.

steps.title: Add a button to increment the store value
steps.instruction: Add an increment function to the store object that updates the value property and calls all subscribed callbacks.
steps.hint: Add a method to the store object that increments this.value and then calls any subscribed callback functions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store object will have an increment method that modifies the value and would notify subscribers when called.
successCriteria: The store object contains an increment function that updates the value property and would notify subscribers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a function to the store, but make sure it properly updates the value property and would notify subscribers when called.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store object doesn't yet have an increment function that updates the value and notifies subscribers.

steps.title: Add increment button to the component
steps.instruction: Inside the StoreDisplay component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Increment' that calls store.increment() when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a button with an onClick handler that invokes store.increment().
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button to trigger an action
<button onClick={() => console.log('Clicked!')}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now have a button that, when clicked, will trigger the store's increment function (once you implement it in the next step).
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Increment' and an onClick handler calling store.increment() is added to the component's return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the text 'Increment' and calls store.increment() when clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button wasn't added correctly. Add a button element with text 'Increment' and an onClick handler that calls store.increment().

steps.title: Add a decrement function to the store
steps.instruction: Add a decrement function to the store object that reduces the value by 1 and notifies subscribers.
steps.hint: Define a function inside the store object that decrements this.value and calls any subscribed callbacks.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store object will have a decrement function that reduces the value and notifies subscribers.
successCriteria: The store object includes a decrement function that reduces this.value and calls subscribed callbacks.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a function, but make sure it decrements the value and notifies subscribers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store object does not have a decrement function that reduces the value and notifies subscribers.

steps.title: Add decrement button to the component
steps.instruction: Add a second button inside your component's return statement that calls the store's decrement function when clicked.
steps.hint: Place the button after the increment button. Use onClick to call store.decrement() directly.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button that triggers a function
<button onClick={() => store.decrement()}>Decrement</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have two buttons: one for incrementing and one for decrementing the store value.
successCriteria: A second button with onClick calling store.decrement() is added to the component's return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it calls store.decrement() when clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The decrement button is missing or not properly connected to the store's decrement function.

steps.title: Add a reset function to the store
steps.instruction: Add a reset function to the store object that sets the value back to 0 and calls any subscriber callbacks.
steps.hint: Define a reset function inside the store object that updates the value property to 0 and invokes any subscribed callbacks.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store object will have a reset function that can be called to reset the value to 0 and notify subscribers.
successCriteria: The store object includes a reset function that sets value to 0 and calls subscriber callbacks.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a reset function, but make sure it properly updates the value property and notifies subscribers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset function is missing or doesn't properly reset the value and notify subscribers. Check the store object structure.

steps.title: Add reset button and complete the UI
steps.instruction: Add a third button to the component that calls the store's reset function when clicked, and organize all three buttons in a clean layout (e.g., with a div wrapper or spacing).
steps.hint: Add a new button element with an onClick handler that calls store.reset(). You can wrap the existing buttons in a div with a class or style for better layout.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with a handler
<button onClick={() => store.reset()}>Reset</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have three buttons (Increment, Decrement, Reset) that update the store value, all displayed in a clean layout.
successCriteria: A third button is added with an onClick handler calling store.reset(), and all buttons are organized in a clean layout (e.g., within a div with styling or spacing).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a reset button, but the layout could be cleaner or the onClick handler might be missing. Ensure the button calls store.reset() and the buttons are well-organized.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset button is missing or not properly connected. Add a button with onClick={() => store.reset()} and organize all buttons in a clean layout.
